security_audit.summary: All 34 static findings are false positives caused by documentation, expected edge APIs, TypeScript syntax, and public runtime metadata. No command execution, secret-file access, reconnaissance, prompt injection, or malicious network intent appears. Semantic review found shared-cache exposure risk and a non-atomic KV rate limiter in instructional examples.

remediation.issue: Cache examples may store personalized or unsuccessful origin responses under shared URL keys.
remediation.suggestion: Bypass authenticated requests and cache only successful responses marked public. Honor private, no-store, and Vary directives.

remediation.issue: KV read-modify-write is non-atomic and eventually consistent, so concurrent requests can bypass the limit.
remediation.suggestion: Use a Durable Object or provider rate-limit primitive with atomic increments, expiration, and validated client identity.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Applications at the Edge
content.value_statement: Edge platforms differ in runtime limits, storage, and deployment behavior. This skill provides practical patterns for routing, authentication, caching, streaming, and rate limiting.
actual_capabilities: Compares Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and Deno Deploy constraints.
Demonstrates geo-routing and request rewriting at edge locations.
Shows JWT authentication patterns for Cloudflare Workers.
Explains KV-based rate limiting and shared edge caching.
Identifies Web APIs available in edge runtimes and unsupported Node.js APIs.
Recommends bundle, streaming, monitoring, CORS, and secret-management practices.
limitations: Platform limits and pricing can change after publication.
Examples are illustrative and require security review before production use.
The skill does not provide deployment commands or complete project scaffolding.
It does not benchmark latency, consistency, or cost for a specific workload.

use_cases.title: Select an Edge Platform
use_cases.description: Compare runtime limits, locations, and free tiers against application requirements.

use_cases.title: Implement Edge Middleware
use_cases.description: Design request routing, localization, experiments, authentication, and origin forwarding.

use_cases.title: Review Traffic Controls
use_cases.description: Assess caching and rate-limiting patterns before production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Edge Platforms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and Deno Deploy for [application]. Prioritize [latency, runtime, cost, or locations]. Recommend one platform.

prompt_templates.title: Design Edge Middleware
prompt_templates.prompt: Design edge middleware for [framework and platform]. Include [routing, localization, or experiments], request flow, required headers, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Edge Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Node.js workload: [description]. Identify incompatible APIs, suitable Web API replacements, storage changes, caching boundaries, and migration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Global Traffic Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production edge architecture for [workload]. Cover authentication, atomic rate limiting, public caching, streaming, observability, consistency, and platform constraints.

output_examples.input: Compare edge platforms for a global personalization API with strict latency requirements.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: Cloudflare Workers. Its broad location coverage and fast isolate startup fit this workload. Validate storage consistency and execution limits before selection.

output_examples.input: Plan middleware for country routing and an A/B experiment.
output_examples.output: Route by trusted platform geography, assign a stable experiment bucket, preserve the bucket in a cookie, and define fallback behavior for missing metadata.

output_examples.input: Review a Worker that caches every successful origin response.
output_examples.output: Cache only responses explicitly marked public. Bypass requests with authorization or private cookies, honor cache directives, and define a bounded cache lifetime.

best_practices: Verify current platform limits and supported APIs before implementation.
Treat authentication, cache policy, and rate limits as separate security boundaries.
Test cold starts, cache behavior, failure paths, and geographic consistency.
anti_patterns: Do not assume Node.js filesystem, process, or native module support.
Do not place personalized responses in a shared cache without explicit safeguards.
Do not use eventually consistent KV counters for strict distributed rate limits.

faq.question: Which edge platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and Deno Deploy.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy an application?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples, but it does not run deployment commands.

faq.question: Can I use Node.js packages at the edge?
faq.answer: Only packages compatible with the selected runtime. Filesystem, child process, and native module dependencies often require replacement.

faq.question: Does it include authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a JWT verification pattern for a Cloudflare Worker.

faq.question: Are the caching examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Add explicit public-cache eligibility, authorization bypasses, cache directives, error handling, and tests.

faq.question: Is KV suitable for strict rate limiting?
faq.answer: Usually not. Strict distributed limits require atomic coordination, such as Durable Objects or a provider rate-limit service.
